opinion_quote: In our opinion, except for the effects of the matters described in the Basis for Qualified Opinion section of our report, the accompanying financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the City of Valencia, Province of Bukidnon as of December 31, 2023, and its financial performance, its cash flows, and its comparison of budget and actual amounts for the year then ended in accordance with International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSASs).

quote: Out of the forty-six (46) audit recommendations from CY 2013 up to CY 2022, twenty-two (22) or 47.83% were fully implemented and twenty-four (24) or 52.17% were not implemented. Detailed tabulation is shown below:
item: Status of Implementation of Prior Years' Audit Recommendations

observation: The City Accountant could not provide the breakdown/ details of the reverted accounts payable amounting P75,240,000.00 as the source of fund for Supplemental Budget No. 02 due to the non-availability of the accounting records from CY 2019 and below thus, noncompliant to Section 111 of PD 1445 hence, the validity of the reverted accounts payable could not be substantiated.
item: Observation 1

observation: The City has Accounts Payable (A/P) from CYs 2020 to 2022 amounting ₱5,195,042.76 for salaries, wages, honoraria, salary differential, hazard pay, gratuity pay, year-end bonus, cash gift, and reimbursements of travelling expenses of several regular, casual and job order employees which are still outstanding as of December 31, 2023 due to improper booking and poor monitoring, in violation of Section 40, Book VI of the Administrative Code and Annex B of COA Circular No. 2015-006 hence, the existence and validity of the A/P balance is doubtful.
item: Observation 2

observation: The validity and accuracy of the Cash-in-Bank account amounting to ₱583,853,343.15 as of December 31, 2023 could not be relied upon due to: a) book reconciling items totaling to ₱98,089,818.4(additions) and ₱69,544,536.19(deductions) to book balances remained unadjusted at year-end; b) Prior-years’ deposits in transit with a total amount of ₱22,224,903.53 still not credited by the bank; and c) non-adjustment of stale checks totaling to ₱279,771.36 which were inconsistent with Section 74 and 112 of PD 1445, Sec. 3.3 COA Circular No. 96-011, and Sections 32 and 59 of the Manual on the New Government accounting System (MNGAS) for LGUs.
item: Observation 3

observation: The balances of the Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) accounts at year end totaling P4,196,736,456.76 did not reconcile with the balance of the Report on Physical Count of PPE amounting P2,482,451.047.19, in violation of Sections 58, 111 and 112 of PD 1445 and COA Circular 2020-006, making the balances of the accounts unreliable.
item: Observation 4

observation: The Property, Plant, and Equipment Ledger Cards (PPLEC) contained incomplete and inaccurate details thus, noncompliant to Sections 114 and 120 of New Government Accounting System (NGAS) for Local Government Units, Sections 111 and 112 of PD 1445 and COA Circular No. 2020-006 which cast doubts on the accuracy and reliability of PPE accounts’ balances in the CY 2023 Statement of Financial Position.
item: Observation 5

observation: The CY 2023 depreciation expenses totaling P27,149,041.24 pertaining to several Property, Plant and Equipment (PPEs) could not be ascertained since: a) beginning balances, loan proceeds, LGU equity and assets which do not meet the definition of PPE were subjected to depreciation, b) there were incomplete details such as date of acquisition, name and location of PPEs in the PPE ledger cards, c) only the name of the contractor/ supplier was indicated as the description of the PPE of the depreciation schedule and, d) various completed assets transferred from Trust Fund directly to equity and, furniture and fixtures were depreciated without breakdown, in contrary to the provisions of Section 13 of IPSAS 17 which rendered the CY 2023 Financial Statements as unreliable.
item: Observation 6

observation: There were Seven Hundred Sixty-Two (762) recorded Property, Plant and Equipment totaling P15,599,428.90 with purchase costs below the P50,000.00 capitalization threshold, in contrary to COA Circular No. 2022-004, hence the PPE accounts’ balances were overstated by the same amount.
item: Observation 7

observation: The existence, validity and accuracy of the reported Inventories’ balances amounting ₱152,462,982.40 could not be ascertained due to non-reconciliation between the records kept by the City Accounting Office (CAO) and the Report of Physical Count of Inventories by the City General Services Office (CGSO) with a variance totaling of ₱115,796,121.40, in violation of section 111 (2) of PD 1445, par. 44 of IPSAS No .12 and, sections 121, 122 and 124 of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Vol. 1 thus, casting doubts on the accuracy and reliability of the Inventories presented in the CY 2023 Statement of Financial Position.
item: Observation 8

observation: The Notes to Financial Statements did not provide adequate disclosures of the material and significant changes of account balances, contrary to the requirements of NGAS Manual and the pertinent disclosure requirements of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS), thereby depriving the intended users of the effective understanding of the Financial Statements.
item: Observation 9

observation: The City Accounting Office and City Budget Office did not install the COA e-NGAS and e-Budget systems after their training held last October 19 to November 4, 2021 thus, noncompliant to COA Circular No. 2004-007 hence, the LGU could not automatically generate the required financial statements and reports when immediately needed by the management and other users of information.
item: Observation 10

observation: The CY 2023 Report on Utilization of Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund had the following errors/discrepancies: a) no breakdown of the continuing appropriation, b) undeducted trust fund expenses and, c) different unutilized balance compared to the balance in the trust fund books thus, non-compliant to Section 111 (2) of PD 1445, thereby casting doubt on the accuracy and reliability of the report.
item: Observation 11

observation: The financial assistance for livelihood projects totaling to ₱800,000.00 granted by the City Government of Valencia to eight (8) NGOs/POs had various deficiencies in violation to Section 4(6) of PD 1445, COA Circular 2012-001, and the executed Memorandum of Agreements governing the transactions which casted doubt on the effectiveness and propriety of granted livelihood assistance.
item: Observation 12

observation: The City Government of Valencia paid salaries to its regular employees amounting to ₱170,122,048.19 until September 2023 with various deficiencies on their supporting Daily Time Records (DTRs) which was noncompliant with Section 4 (6 & 7) of PD 1445, CSC Memorandum Circular No. 21, series of 1991 and Sec. 194 of the Government Accounting and Auditing Manual Vol. I, thereby casting doubt on the accuracy and validity of the salaries paid for that period.
item: Observation 13

observation: Basic internal control on segregation of duties was not properly observed by allowing the HR department to handle both the creation of payroll and at the same time given the access to upload payroll data for the crediting of salaries and other employee benefits through Landbank weAccess for CY 2023 amounting to ₱491,254,403.58, which was not in accordance to Section 50 of the Government Accounting and Auditing Manual (GAAM) Vol III, and Internal Control Standards for the Philippine Public Sector (ICSPPS) prescribed under COA Circular 2018-003, thereby exposing the government funds to risk of possible losses and misappropriation.
item: Observation 14

observation: CY 2023 Terminal Leave Benefits claims totaling P4,930,708.09 were incompletely supported with the required documents thus, noncompliant to Section 51.13 of COA Circular No. 2012-001 thereby casting doubt on propriety of the claims.
item: Observation 15

observation: Employees who monetized fifty percent (50%) or more of their accumulated leave credits did not provide justification for their claims thus, non-compliant to CSC Memorandum Circular No. 16, s. 2002 and COA Circulars No. 2012-001 which cast doubt on the propriety of the claims.
item: Observation 16

observation: CY 2023 procurements totaling ₱122,258,110.58 were unsupported with various required documents, in violation to Section 4(6) of Presidential Decree 1445 and Republic Act 9184, thereby casting doubts on the regularity of the transactions.
item: Observation 17

observation: Various goods procured by the City Government of Valencia totaling to ₱20,710,334.50 were paid without warranty security, in violation to Sec. 62.1 of RA 9184 which exposes the city to the risk and difficulty of recovering damages in case of defects on the procured goods.
item: Observation 18

observation: The CY 2023 procured drugs and medicines totaling P5,376,620.13 were unsupported with the required documents prior to disbursement thus, noncompliant to COA Circulars No. 2012-001 and 2023-004, thereby casting doubts on propriety of the transactions.
item: Observation 19

observation: All 100% completed projects with approved time extensions were not supported with the written consent of the bondsmen for the extension of the validity of the performance security, in violation of Section 39.5 and Section 11 of Annex E of the Revised IRR of R.A. 9184 thus, all performance securities for the faithful performance of the contractors’ obligations may not fully cover the approved time extensions.
